newsitem.title: MALI: France says it will help Mali deter emigration.
newsitem.headline: France says it will help Mali deter emigration.

text.p: France, keen to curb illegal immigration from Africa, has told Mali that it will help promote projects in the impoverished western region of Kayes to prevent people leaving for a better life abroad.

Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain told reporters after visiting the region late on Tuesday that the trip had given him a clear insight into the "considerable" task that needed to be undertaken there.
"The creation of local projects is an adequate solution to curb immigration, develop the region and keep its people occupied," he said after talks with President Alpha Oumar Konare.
Godfrain, who later left for home, said that France Caisse Francaise de Developpement investment arm and France's cooperation departments would be put in charge of the affair.

The trip was expected to smooth relations with Mali after France deported more than 100 African illegal immigrants last month, mostly Malians. Some were expelled by force from a Paris church, drawing criticism from rights groups.
Human rights groups in Mali angered by the expulsions had called for Godfrains's two-day visit to be cancelled but it passed off without major incident.
